metaData.originalTitle: Codex 日志正在燃烧你的 SSD
metaData.title: Codex Logs Are Burning Your SSD
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the SSD write amplification issue caused by the OpenAI Codex logging system writing heavily at TRACE level to SQLite, presenting a chain of evidence, risk stratification, immediate mitigation measures, and upstream fix directions.
metaData.summary: This article dissects the logging system issue in OpenAI Codex: its persistent SQLite log sink defaults to accepting TRACE-level logs from all targets, bypassing the user-set `RUST_LOG=warn` filter, leading to continuous high-frequency writes to `logs_2.sqlite` and its WAL file during streaming output. From the source code perspective, the article explains the write amplification mechanism (WAL mode, multiple indexes, insert-prune cycle), cites data from open issues on GitHub such as #17320 and #28224 (e.g., 5 MiB/s write rate, extrapolated 640 TB writes per year), and points out that the file size users see may differ dramatically from actual SSD write volume. The author stratifies the risks to avoid over-panicking, while emphasizing that Mac users face higher risk. The article evaluates three mitigation measures circulating online (SQLite trigger to block inserts, symlink to /tmp or a ramdisk, migrating the SQLite directory to an external drive), detailing their limitations and proper usage. Finally, it proposes the truly necessary upstream fixes: narrowing the default filter, sanitizing protocol payloads, and adding a global size cap. The article cites specific code lines and issue links, with rigorous reasoning and practical advice.

mainPoints.point: Codex's SQLite log sink defaults to allowing TRACE-level logs from all targets, leading to massive amounts of useless data being written to disk.
mainPoints.explanation: Even with `RUST_LOG=warn` set, this sink has an independent filter chain, causing high-frequency noise such as WebSocket/SSE payloads to be persistently written to disk.

mainPoints.point: SQLite's WAL mode and insert-prune cycle cause the file size to remain stable while the underlying write volume is enormous.
mainPoints.explanation: After inserting a new row, index updates and old row deletions are triggered, resulting in actual SSD writes far exceeding the net file growth. Extrapolated yearly writes can reach 640 TB.

mainPoints.point: The popular online mitigations—trigger blocking and symlinking to /tmp—each have serious limitations.
mainPoints.explanation: The trigger sacrifices feedback logs and is not a long-term solution; macOS's /tmp is not a ramdisk, making symlinks ineffective. The correct approach is to use `sqlite_home` to migrate to an external drive or wait for an upstream fix.

mainPoints.point: Upstream fixes should focus on boundary control for persistent logs.
mainPoints.explanation: This includes setting a stricter default filter level, sanitizing payloads, adding a global size cap, and a configuration toggle. Users should not rely on workarounds.

keyQuotes: Diagnostic logs can exist, but they must have clear levels, sampling, sanitization, retention, and size boundaries.
Debugging information can be abundant, but what is persisted by default must be minimal, stable, explainable, and controllable.
Stopping the bleeding can be done with a trigger, `sqlite_home` migration, or WAL cleanup. Curing the disease can only happen within Codex's own SQLite log sink.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: Can AI Write Code in Truly "Mission-Critical" Backend Systems?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article shares the complete methodology—Harness Engineering—practiced by Tencent's CDN LEGO team for AI coding in ultra-large-scale, high-reliability backend systems. Through a five-layer architecture, three key levers (context, constraints, feedback), and multi-model adversarial code review, they built an engineering system that enables AI to safely and controllably produce high-quality code.

relatedArticles.title: On Agent Memory
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article delves into the essence, architectural philosophy, and governance challenges of AI Agent memory systems, arguing that true memory is not simple storage and retrieval, but the continuous reinterpretation, hierarchical governance, and skill solidification of past experiences, while critiquing the common misconception of equating RAG or long context with memory.

relatedArticles.title: A Practical Guide to 'Progressive Spec' for AI Coding in 2026
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article proposes a 'Progressive Spec' framework for AI coding environments, leveraging structured documentation to drive AI collaboration and balance development standards with execution efficiency.

relatedArticles.title: Deep Dive: Architectural Decay & Loop Engineering
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article delves into the nature, causes, and countermeasures of system architectural decay from a software engineering practice perspective, proposing an engineering framework for continuous entropy reduction in the AI Agent era through Loop Engineering.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: How I Spent a Week Boosting AI Coding Rate to 90% in an Enterprise App
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces Harness Engineering, a new AI coding paradigm that elevates the AI code rate of an enterprise Java application from 25% to over 90% by building a four-element system of rules, skills, knowledge, and change management.

relatedArticles.title: Deep Dive: Claude Code Source Code
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a deep dive into the reverse-engineered source code of Claude Code, revealing its agent architecture based on Harness Engineering, with a focus on core mechanisms like state persistence, tool scheduling, and the system prompt control plane.

relatedArticles.title: The Essence of Agent Memory Architecture
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the architectural essence of Agent Memory systems, arguing that the core challenge lies in governance rather than capacity, and systematically proposes a complete design framework comprising four modeling objects, a six-dimensional basic memory unit, and three core links.

relatedArticles.title: Rethinking Development Infrastructure: When Agents Become First-Class Citizens
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article proposes a unified framework of 'intent-driven + code precipitation', arguing that agents do not change the fundamental structure of software evolution but compress the 'intent → code' cycle from months/weeks to minutes, and thus deduces that development infrastructure must shift from People-Oriented to Agent-Oriented design principles.

relatedArticles.title: AI R&D Automation: Wiki Knowledge Base + Skill Pack
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how to build a continuously growing team knowledge base and a supporting expert skill pack based on the LLM-Wiki model and the Obsidian platform to achieve AI-driven R&D automation.

relatedArticles.title: A Brief Discussion on AI Programming
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article delves into the paradigm shift in AI programming, arguing that when the marginal cost of code generation approaches zero, the core of software engineering will shift from 'writing code' to 'governing AI production systems,' making specifications, constraints, and verification systems more important assets than the code itself.
